label: James V. Forrestal
narrative: James V. Forrestal was Secretary of the Navy until September 1947 and then the first Secretary of Defense, from 17 September 1947 to 28 March 1949, under the National Security Act of 1947 that created the office. He reaches this board as the addressee of the memorandum the whole MJ-12 corpus is built on and as the subject of a recurring claim that his death was concealed. Two things about him are documented and one is not. Documented: the office and its dates, and the statutory requirement that its holder be a civilian, which contradicts the 1987 document's repeated description of him as 'General James V. Forestall'. Not documented from here: the United States Navy board of investigation into his death of 1949, the Willcutts Report, which could not be opened at the Internet Archive, in the National Archives catalogue, or through the university finding aid that a search named; the claim that his medical records are sealed is therefore neither confirmed nor refuted on this board.
